sample_unit: cases (real-world test set: 46 irreducible and 802 reducible)

links.outcome: Radiologist diagnostic performance with versus without AI assistance
links.effect: Assistive use significantly improved radiologists' performance (all P < 0.01): AUC improvements of 0.095-0.072, balanced accuracy gains of 8.6-11.7%, specificity increases of 18.7-22.6%.
links.quote: When used as an assistive tool, the model significantly improved radiologists' diagnostic performance (all P < 0.01), with AUC improvements of 0.095-0.072, balanced accuracy gains of 8.6-11.7%, and specificity increases of 18.7-22.6%.

links.outcome: AI model AUC compared with radiologists and other methods on same data
links.effect: Model AUC 0.89 vs intermediate radiologist 0.804 (P < 0.001) and senior radiologist 0.842 (P = 0.108); outperformed comparative methods (AUC ranges 0.823-0.877 and 0.634-0.826).
links.quote: The model demonstrated superior performance compared with that of the intermediate radiologist (AUC: 0.89 vs. 0.804; P < 0.001) and comparable performance to that of a senior radiologist (AUC: 0.89 vs. 0.842; P = 0.108).

screen.reason: The study includes a reader study evaluating the diagnostic performance of radiologists with and without AI assistance.

primary.practice: AI-assisted clinical decision support vs unassisted radiologist interpretation
